name: OpenAIEmbeddingService
title: Embedding Service
description: Turns text into vector embeddings for semantic search
whenToUse: Turn text into vectors so records can be indexed for and retrieved by semantic search: the backend a vector store calls to embed both what it stores and what it later queries. Model and dimensions are selectable. Attach via a service edge to that consumer; it is not a data-flow step.

normalize.title: Normalize Embeddings
normalize.description: Normalize to unit length (recommended for cosine similarity)

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: openai
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# The package envelope, and now the ONLY envelope: this package is fully
# declarative. All five nodes are manifests, there is no src/ and no package.json,
# so nothing here is built, published or imported. The retired TypeScript sits at
# _legacy/nodes/openai for reference.
#
# A code node of the same type always beats a manifest at load, which is what made
# migrating one node at a time possible. With the code gone there is nothing left
# to beat these.

name: openai
displayName: OpenAI
description: OpenAI integration for Unoverse
version: 1.3.0
category: ai
# First-party. The marketplace shows this on every node the package registers, so
# "who am I trusting with this credential" is answerable without leaving the screen.
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749262616/gravity/icons/ChatGPT-Logo.svg.webp

features:
  - GPT-5.6 models
  - Live two-way voice, with the model interruptible mid-sentence
  - Streaming responses
  - Function/tool calling
  - Text embeddings
  - Structured JSON output
  - Vision (image inputs)
  - Realtime voice calls with transcripts of both sides

# The ONLY hosts this package's nodes may call. The executor refuses anything else.
#
# A manifest cannot execute code, but without this it could still say "send this
# credential to evil.example", which is exfiltration with no code at all. One short
# reviewable list is what makes a manifest safe to accept from someone else.
allowedHosts:
  - api.openai.com

# Executor capabilities every manifest node here depends on. Deploy REFUSES this
# package if the target universe's executor cannot satisfy them, so a manifest can
# never name a capability that only exists on a newer executor.
# `ws` and the raised floor came with OpenAIRealtimeVoice (2026-08-12): a realtime session is a
# SOCKET, and the duplex runtime that holds one open landed in executor 1.5.0.
requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [sse, json, ws]
  # OpenAIAgent keeps its OpenAI conversation id between runs. A universe whose executor
  # cannot do this would otherwise read a permanently cold cache and start a new
  # conversation every turn: memory that silently never remembers.
  state: [read, merge]
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"

credentials.openAICredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from
# plugin-base/src/credentials/openai.ts, which this package re-exports today.
#
# Values live where they already live: encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe,
# and in the developer's own .env locally. That is why a manifest is safe to commit.
#
# Nodes reference this by NAME. At run time context.credentials holds EVERY credential
# in the workflow keyed by name, and the executor must select by name, never by
# scanning for the first object with an apiKey: openAICredential, apolloCredential,
# hunterCredential and searchapiCredential all expose one, so a scan silently
# authenticates against the wrong service the moment a second is added to the
# workflow (04-credentials.md).

name: openAICredential
displayName: OpenAI
description: Credentials for OpenAI API
documentationUrl: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your OpenAI API key
    placeholder: sk-...

  - name: organizationId
    displayName: Organization ID
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Your OpenAI organization ID (optional)
    placeholder: org-...

  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Custom API endpoint (optional)
    default: https://api.openai.com/v1

shared.endpoints.yaml:
# OpenAI's endpoints. Written once here rather than seven times across the nodes.
#
# No chat/completions: every node uses the Responses API. `messages` is the legacy shape.
#
#   url: { $ref: ../../shared/endpoints.yaml#/responses }

responses: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
embeddings: https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings

# A CONVERSATION is OpenAI's own server-side memory: a durable id you mint once and then
# name on every response. Items are prepended to the request and the turn's input and
# output are appended back, so history never travels from here and is never stored here.
# Minted with POST and an empty body; the reply carries the id.
#
# NO CALLER SINCE 2026-08-23. OpenAIAgent was the only one and now chains with
# previous_response_id instead. Kept because the URL is a fact about the vendor rather
# than about any node, and re-deriving it is the sort of small cost that argues for
# leaving a one-line constant alone. Nothing here decides which mechanism a node uses —
# each declares that next to its own reason (shared/tools.yaml).
conversations: https://api.openai.com/v1/conversations
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical GPT model list, the SINGLE source every OpenAI node references,
# organised by TIER. Transcribed from src/shared/models.ts.
#
# Models come in three tiers. A new generation is a one-line edit per tier here, and
# every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# The DATA lives here. The FALLBACK LOGIC (resolveModel: a retired id resolves to the
# current best model in its tier, so replacing a generation cannot break a saved
# workflow) is computation, not description, so it belongs to the executor. It is
# declared per config field as `resolver: modelTier`, not written here.

# One current model per tier. Update these three lines when a new generation ships.
byTier:
  small: gpt-5.6-luna # cost-optimized, high-volume
  medium: gpt-5.6-terra # balanced intelligence/cost, the default
  large: gpt-5.6 # frontier, complex work

# Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
default: gpt-5.6-terra

# The NARRATOR: the model that writes an agent's short "thinking" status line. A separate
# concern from the model doing the work, so it is named separately.
#
# Deliberately NOT the 5.6 family: 5.6 is luna/sol/terra with no nano tier, and this call
# exists to reach the user fast, not to be clever. Measured 2026-07-26, three runs each,
# same prompt and schema:
#
#   gpt-5.4-nano   avg 1137ms   [1470, 905, 1035]
#   gpt-5.6-luna   avg 2043ms   [1846, 2337, 1945]
#
# Luna is ~80% slower and less consistent for lines that are indistinguishable in quality.
# Re-measure when a faster small model ships; never assume.
narrator: gpt-5.4-nano


# The picker's options. Listed large first so the strongest reads first.
enum:
  - gpt-5.6
  - gpt-5.6-terra
  - gpt-5.6-luna

enumNames:
  - Sol (Frontier, complex work)
  - Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
  - Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)
shared.realtimeTools.yaml:
# The OpenAI REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   offer, not      Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST, so a list that GREW since the
#   toolsInto       last turn is re-sent for free and there is nothing to declare. A socket sends
#                   it once at the handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — which is
#                   what `offer` below is. Same fact, two shapes: `toolsInto` names a request
#                   field, `offer` names a whole message.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown. `tools` is the whole live list, already in the
# envelope `tool` above produces.
#
# ONLY `tools`: session.update MERGES (verified live 2026-08-12), so instructions, modalities,
# voice and turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session block would be a second
# copy of the handshake, free to drift. Safe at any moment — the vendor gates `response.create` on
# an idle conversation, never session.update.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { type: 'realtime', tools: tools } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]
shared.tools.yaml:
# The OpenAI Responses tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does NOT belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it
# does not belong copied into every node either. It belongs here: shared by every OpenAI
# node, imported whole.
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#     maxTurns: 5            # local keys layer on top and win
#
# When OpenAI changes how a function call is expressed, exactly one file changes.
# NO SDK. This is the wire format, described as data.

# How ONE tool is offered to the model. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }
toolsInto: tools

# How a call ARRIVES in the stream.
call:
  match: response.output_item.done
  when: "return response.item.type === 'function_call'"
  id: "return response.item.call_id"
  name: "return response.item.name"
  arguments: "return response.item.arguments"

# How ONE result goes BACK. `call` is { id, name, output }.
result: >-
  return { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output }
resultsInto: input

# Always auto: which tool to reach for is carried by the tool DESCRIPTIONS, never by
# forcing a choice.
choiceInto: tool_choice
choice: auto

# NO `continuity` HERE, and that is deliberate. How a turn reaches the one before it is a
# per-node CHOICE on this vendor, not one wire format, because OpenAI offers two and
# REFUSES both at once:
#
#   previous_response_id   chains response to response. A new id every turn, known only
#                          after the turn ends. Declared by OpenAIStream, and since
#                          2026-08-23 by OpenAIAgent too — which now outlives a single
#                          execution by REMEMBERING that id (continuity.remember) rather
#                          than by holding a durable one.
#   conversation           a durable id, minted once and named on every turn, with the API
#                          keeping the history. No caller today.
#
# Sending both is `mutually_exclusive_parameters`, a hard 400 (confirmed against the live
# API 2026-08-12). So a node that names a conversation must NOT inherit continuity, and
# this file cannot decide for both. Each declares its own, next to the reason it chose it.

files.api/service.yaml:
# No `request` and no `events`: this node has no workflow channel. Only `provides`, the
# methods a consumer calls over a service edge. Transcribed from
# src/OpenAIEmbeddingService/service/{createEmbedding,embeddings}.ts.
#
# The service channel hands a value BACK to its caller rather than emitting on output
# connectors, which is why a method says `returns` and there is no events table here.
# The shape is otherwise the same one idea as the workflow channel: a call frames its own
# reply (transport, error), and the method says what it hands back.
#
# `config.model` carries "<model>:<dims>", so both methods split it. Doing that in the
# expression rather than adding an executor capability is the right call: it is
# description of THIS service's config convention, not computation the platform owes
# every node.

createEmbedding:
  description: Embed one piece of text and return its vector.

  calls:
    - name: embed
      method: POST
      url: { $ref: endpoints#embeddings }
      credential:
        scheme: bearer
        token: "{{ credentials.openAICredential.apiKey }}"
      body: >-
        return {
          model: config.model.split(':')[0],
          input: params.text,
          dimensions: parseInt(config.model.split(':')[1], 10) || 1536
        }
      retry:
        attempts: 3
        backoff: exponential
        on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

      transport: json

      # A 200 carrying an error body must not read as success.
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error.message"

  # Unit-normalised unless switched off, because cosine similarity assumes it.
  # The norm is recomputed per element rather than bound to a name: the sandbox has
  # no assignment, by design. 1536 floats against an HTTP round trip is free.
  returns: >-
    return {
      embedding: config.normalize === false
        ? response.data[0].embedding
        : response.data[0].embedding.map(x =>
            x / Math.sqrt(response.data[0].embedding.reduce((a, b) => a + b * b, 0))),
      dimensions: response.data[0].embedding.length,
      model: response.model
    }

createBatchEmbeddings:
  description: Embed many texts in one call and return their vectors in order.

  calls:
    - name: embed
      method: POST
      url: { $ref: endpoints#embeddings }
      credential:
        scheme: bearer
        token: "{{ credentials.openAICredential.apiKey }}"
      # The endpoint takes an array for `input`, so a batch is one request, not N.
      body: >-
        return {
          model: config.model.split(':')[0],
          input: params.texts,
          dimensions: parseInt(config.model.split(':')[1], 10) || 1536
        }
      retry:
        attempts: 3
        backoff: exponential
        on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

      transport: json

      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error.message"

  # Ordered by index: the API does not guarantee response order matches input order.
  # Rebuilt by index rather than sorted, because `sort` mutates and the expression
  # sandbox allows no mutating method. This method had never been run, so the rejected
  # `sort` would have failed the first real batch.
  returns: >-
    return {
      embeddings: response.data
        .map((_, i) => response.data.find(d => d.index === i))
        .map(d => config.normalize === false
          ? d.embedding
          : d.embedding.map(x => x / Math.sqrt(d.embedding.reduce((a, b) => a + b * b, 0)))),
      dimensions: response.data[0].embedding.length,
      model: response.model
    }
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model]

  properties:
    # Model and dimensions travel as ONE value, "<model>:<dims>", because they are not
    # independent: text-embedding-3-small cannot do 3072. One picker cannot express an
    # invalid pair, two could.
    model:
      type: string
      title: Embedding Model
      description: Select model and dimensions
      enum:
        - text-embedding-3-small:512
        - text-embedding-3-small:1536
        - text-embedding-3-large:1024
        - text-embedding-3-large:1536
        - text-embedding-3-large:3072
        - text-embedding-ada-002:1536
      enumNames:
        - text-embedding-3-small (512D) - Fast
        - text-embedding-3-small (1536D) - Higher quality
        - text-embedding-3-large (1024D) - Balanced
        - text-embedding-3-large (1536D) - Best quality
        - text-embedding-3-large (3072D) - Maximum
        - text-embedding-ada-002 (1536D) - Legacy
      default: text-embedding-3-large:1536

    normalize:
      type: boolean
      title: Normalize Embeddings
      description: Normalize to unit length (recommended for cosine similarity)
      default: true
      ui:widget: toggle
ui:order: [model, normalize]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

# NO inputs and NO outputs, deliberately. This node is never triggered by the graph.
# Consumers attach a service edge and call its methods; it answers them and hands back a
# value. The workflow channel and the service channel do not cross (08-mcp-services.md).

serviceConnectors:
  - name: embeddingService
    description: Provides embedding generation services
    serviceType: embedding
    isService: true
    methods:
      - createEmbedding
      - createBatchEmbeddings

credentials:
  - name: openAICredential
    required: true
    displayName: OpenAI API
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

# Transcribed from src/OpenAIEmbeddingService/node/index.ts.
#
# A PURE SERVICE node. It is never triggered by the graph and has no inputs or
# outputs; other nodes call its methods over a service edge and it hands back a value.
# That is why api.yaml has `provides` and no `request`/`response`.

type: OpenAIEmbeddingService
kind: PromiseNode

# HOW THE CANVAS DRAWS IT. A pure service node has NO connectors, so the ordinary card draws
# input and output dots that can never carry anything and invites someone to wire it into the
# data flow rather than attaching it to a consumer.
template: service

name: Embedding Service
category: AI
color: "#2F6F66"

# "OpenAI embedding service" restated the node's own name and told a reader nothing.
description: Turns text into vector embeddings for semantic search

# The model names were in the opening, where doc 14 wants the JOB. Detail moved back and
# the service-edge fact stays last, which is the resolution for a provider node.
whenToUse: >-
  Turn text into vectors so records can be indexed for and retrieved by semantic search:
  the backend a vector store calls to embed both what it stores and what it later queries.
  Model and dimensions are selectable. Attach via a service edge to that consumer; it is
  not a data-flow step.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # An embedding IS deterministic for the same text, model and dimensions, and it is a
  # pure read with no side effect. The one node here that genuinely earns memoization.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# A pure service node has nothing to trigger, so the fixture CALLS it the way a
# consumer would rather than feeding inputs.
testData:
  config:
    model: text-embedding-3-large:1024
    normalize: true

  call:
    method: createEmbedding
    params:
      text: A workflow engine coordinates the execution of steps.

  expect:
    # The dimensions actually requested, not whatever the model defaults to.
    embedding: "return output.dimensions === 1024 && output.embedding.length === 1024"
    # Unit length, since normalize is on. Floating point, so within a tolerance.
    model: >-
      return Math.abs(Math.sqrt(output.embedding.reduce((a, b) => a + b * b, 0)) - 1) < 0.001
